events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
Safety screen first. The driver's chat message at 09:54 reads "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it" [F11]; the complaint also alleges the driver threatened the rider in chat [F12 records three timestamped messages, so the chat is complete and this line is the driver's own words, F9–F11]. Read in context this is not a pickup arrangement or a complaint about lateness: it is a conditional threat of pursuit and retaliation aimed at the rider, which is intimidation/harassment of the other party under SAFE-1. I therefore record safety_concern = confirmed, basis F11 (with F9–F11, F12 for the complete record), and under SAFE-1 I do not decide the case: ruling = escalate, escalate = true.

The underlying fee dispute is otherwise clean on the record. cancelled_by = driver [F4], so NS-0 routes the $6.61 fee to NS-1. All three NS-1 elements are marked ✓ by the trace and are supported by the facts: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45 [F6], at that moment 38 m from pickup, within the 200 m radius [F6][F1], and stayed inside the radius for 3 min 40 s (220 s) until cancelling at 09:54:25 [F6][F4], exceeding the 180 s threshold. The platform-arrival variant at 09:49:50 with 4 min 35 s within 200 m [F2][F5] corroborates. On those elements alone NS-1 would make the $6.61 fee stand (no_action). The rider's own "2 min, coming" at 09:52 [F10] and the absence of any traffic cause [F14][F15] leave no NS-2 or RD-4 argument open.

I cannot, however, execute that outcome at this stage: SAFE-1 removes the case from automated adjudication, and the human reviewer must decide whether the threat affects the fee/account treatment (and whether the driver's conduct warrants action independently of the fare). No amount is computed: the fee computation is a fee dispute, and no_action/escalate carry amount = null. Flag_account is not set: NS-2's flag condition (tap made from outside the pickup radius) is not met [F6][F1], and RD-6 does not apply to a no-show case (route disputes upheld = 0) [F18]; the driver's prior upheld no-show dispute [F18] is a profile fact and cannot decide anything on its own. Evidence is sufficient: the chat is complete and timestamped [F12], the GPS trace covers the wait without a hole [F2][F6], and cancellation author and time are recorded [F4], so every element I needed is settled by the record.
